FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DOCUMENT. The materials, laboratories and measurements below are invented for software testing.

Comparative screening of spinel and layered oxygen evolution catalysts

Summary. We screened six catalysts, including CM-2 and LX-4, in a single three-electrode cell under identical conditions to remove laboratory-to-laboratory variation.

Method. Each catalyst was loaded at 0.5 mg cm-2 on glassy carbon and measured in 1 M KOH at 25 °C with a rotating disk at 1600 rpm. Linear sweep voltammograms were recorded at 5 mV s-1.

Results. At a fixed potential of 1.6 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, CM-2 delivered 62 mA cm-2 and LX-4 delivered 95 mA cm-2. The other four catalysts delivered between 8 and 40 mA cm-2. The ranking was reproducible across two independent catalyst batches.

Limitations. Rotating disk measurements at low loading do not represent device operation. The current densities here should not be compared directly with flow-cell or membrane-electrode-assembly results, which use different loadings, temperatures and cell voltages.
